title: Embeddings bulk endpoint deprecation transition playbook and migration safety gates
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and phased migration plan for deprecating the legacy /v1/embeddings/bulk endpoint. The goal is to provide a low-friction migration path to the unified embeddings endpoint (/v2/embeddings) and SDK helpers while minimizing customer disruption and measurable regression in embedding quality or throughput. Scope includes migration messaging, SDK helper changes, telemetry gates, rollout schedule, billing and quota mapping, and post-migration validation checklists. Not in scope: model architecture changes, core embedding model retraining, or unrelated console UX work.
acceptance_criteria: Public deprecation announcement drafted and scheduled at least 12 weeks before enforced sunset
Client migration guide with example requests for the top three client languages (Python, Node, Go) published in docs, including code samples for batching and error handling
SDK helpers released to translate bulk payloads into the new multiplexed batch format and shipped in major SDKs with semver minor bump
Server-side compatibility shim for bulk calls created as a limited-duration safety net and instrumented for latency/cost impact
Telemetry dashboards showing: incoming bulk traffic by customer, error rates, average request size, and cost delta between bulk vs new endpoint
Rollout plan with clear rollback and capacity fallback documented and approved by Eng and SRE
No critical customer has open blocking tickets preventing migration by final deprecation date (exceptions require exec signoff)
migration_timeline: Week 0 (2026-03-01): Publish intent to deprecate with FAQ and recommended migration timeline (12 weeks)
Week 2: SDK helper alpha release and internal dogfooding with three high-usage customers
Week 4: Public SDK helpers GA and docs published; begin targeted customer outreach
Week 8: Start phased traffic shift test for friendly customers (5% of original bulk traffic routed to new endpoint) with telemetry gates
Week 12 (2026-05-15): Enforced deprecation: bulk endpoint returns 410 for new requests after notice period; compatibility shim enters maintenance-only mode for a further 4 weeks
rollout_plan: Phase A - Communication: Public blog + status page + email to top 200 bulk users, include migration docs and code snippets
Phase B - SDKs & Tools: Release SDK helpers and CLI migration tool; publish samples for converting bulk inputs to batched requests
Phase C - Early adopters: Invite 10 high-volume customers to test; monitor latency, p99s, cost per 1k tokens and embedding similarity metrics
Phase D - Gradual enforcement: Increase enforcement bandwidth while monitoring telemetry gates and error budgets
Phase E - Sunset: Remove write paths in compatibility shim after maintenance window and finalize billing reconciliation
rollback_plan: If p50 latency increases > 40% for 2 consecutive measurement windows, pause enforcement and reopen the compatibility shim for writes
If error rate for migrated customers > 5% for 24h, rollback SDK change via patch release and notify customers
Maintain a short-term compatibility tier that can be re-enabled per-customer for up to 4 weeks after sunset on exec approval
monitoring_and_telemetry: Create dashboard: bulk_deprecation_overview (traffic, errors, latency, cost delta)
Track embedding quality regressions via similarity drift on seeded eval set (weekly run)
Instrument SDK helper adoption via telemetry tag 'sdk_migration_v1'
Set automated alerts: bulk_endpoint_traffic_drop > 90% by week 10 (warn), error_rate_migrants > 3% (critical)
client_sdk_changes: Add Embeddings.batch_from_bulk(payload) helper to Python/Node/Go SDKs with clear migration examples
Return warnings in client logs when legacy bulk schema is used (deprecation header + migration link)
Publish migration CLI: rdx migrate-embeddings --from-bulk --to-batched --concurrency N
Coordinate SDK releases with docs publish (same day) and include compatibility notes in changelogs
notes: Stakeholders: PM (Asha), Eng leads (Carlos Mendes, Priya Shah), SRE (Ivy Chen), DX (Evan Li)
Eng must provide performance characterization for the multiplexed batch format before Week 4
Billing mapping: QA needed to ensure per-embedding unit billing parity for customers that used bulk payloads
Legal review recommended for customer contracts that explicitly reference the deprecated endpoint
